narrative.title: The One-Question Corridor Descent
narrative.scenario: A records archive is arranged so every corridor box answers a single question: is the file you want smaller or larger than me? Starting at the entrance box, each answer permanently discards one wing of the archive, so a handful of questions — not a shelf-by-shelf hunt — lands the clerk on the exact box, or confirms the file was never filed here.
narrative.inputFormat: A binary search tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child) and an integer val to locate.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the subtree rooted at the found node, serialized as a level-order array with trailing nulls trimmed. Return an empty array if val is absent.

testCases.explanation: The search drops left of 4 and stops at 2, returning 2's subtree.
Neither wing can hold 5, so the descent runs off the tree empty-handed.

hintLevels: Level 1: Never scan — at every box ask 'smaller or larger?' and throw away the other wing forever.
Level 2: Equal values stop the walk; smaller-than-me means go left, larger means go right.
Level 3: Falling off a leaf without a match is the certified 'absent' signal — one descent, no revisits.
